Chapter 9: Vastu in Community and Shared Spaces.
You know, a lot of what we’ve talked about with Vastu centers on our own homes, but these same ideas work wonders in shared and community spaces too. Think about offices, schools, or even neighborhoods—how we arrange these places can shape how we come together, collaborate, and feel connected as a group.
The first thing to keep in mind? Every group has its own unique rhythm and needs. For example, a school might really thrive when classrooms face east, helping students tap into learning and creativity. Meanwhile, a community center could use the north side as a welcoming zone, perfect for gatherings and new connections.
So, how can you actually bring Vastu principles into these shared spaces? Here are a few simple ways:
Try keeping the center of a room or building open. It’s a bit like having your own little village square—open centers make it easier for people to move around and interact naturally.
Make entrances clear and inviting. A clutter-free, welcoming entryway instantly sets a positive mood and makes everyone feel like they belong.
Think about creating zones for different activities. Maybe you have a quiet study area in the northeast, while lively discussions or teamwork happen in the northwest. This helps everyone find the right space for what they’re doing.
And don’t forget about symbols of unity. Adding things like art, plants, or shared objects in the Brahmasthan—the very center—can really boost that sense of belonging and shared purpose.
Now, if you’re looking at workplaces, Vastu can do a lot for teamwork and productivity. Simply aligning workstations with helpful directions or making sure shared spaces are bright and welcoming can make a huge difference. In neighborhoods, setting up a community garden or gathering spot in the north or east can quickly become a hub of energy and connection.
Here’s something to remember: treat these shared spaces with the same care and thoughtfulness you’d give your own home. The environment isn’t just shaping individual experiences—it’s nurturing the whole community spirit.
When you apply Vastu with intention, you’re not just making things more functional. You’re creating places that feel truly alive, supportive, and inspiring for everyone.
